texts.preamble: Deepika Bhatiya vs Pulkit Aggarwal on 31 October, 2023 In The Court Of Sh.Shailender Malik, Presiding Officer: Motor Accident Claims Tribunal-02, Shahdara, Karkardooma Courts, Delhi Mact No.1373/2016 Deepika Bhatia R/o 169, West Azad Nagar, Delhi. ... Petitioner Versus (1)Pulkit Aggarwal R/o 138, Surya Niketan, Delhi-110092. (2)Vinod Kumar Agarwal r/o 138, Surya Niketan Delhi-110092. (3)National Insurance Company Limited ... Respondents Date of Institution : 12.08.2015 Date of Arguments : 20.10.2023 Date of pronouncement : 31.10.2023 Awar D 1.
texts.facts: Proceedings have arisen from filing of DAR in FIR No. 437/15 of PS Anand Vihar, registered u/s 279/338 IPC, in respect of an accident dated 21.06.2015 wherein petitioner Deepika Bhatia suffered grievous injuries including severe head injury. As per the facts, on 21.06.2015, at about 06 :15 PM injured/petitioner Deepika was crossing the road near cross river mall, near Karkardooma courts. Respondent no. 1 Pulkit Aggarwal was allegedly driving the offending vehicle bearing registration no. DL-14CM-4444 Maruti Suzuki Ertiga, in a rash and negligent manner and hit the petitioner which resulted in MACT No.1373/2016 Page 1 causing of grievous injuries including head injury. Petitioner was taken to Dr. Hedgewar hospital, where her MLC no. 1950/15 was prepared and later she was shifted to MAX superspecialty hospital Patparganj. 2. In response to the DAR, owner and driver filed the reply / written statement wherein it is denied that accident took place due to rash and reckless driving of respondent no. 1. It is pleaded that vehicle in question was fully insured with National Insurance co. ltd. Vide policy no. 35101031156136605630 valid from 30.04.2015 to 29.04.2016. It is stated that driver was having valid DL. Reply/ written statement has also been filed by respondent no.3/ insurance company, wherein insurance company took all the plea in terms of Section 134 (c), 147/149, 157,66 nad 88 of Motor Vehicle Act and further pleaded that insurance company reserved right to take appropriate defence as per Section 170 M V Act. It is not disputed however, that the vehicle in question was duly insured with respondent no. 3. It is pleaded that petitioner is required to prove the rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle. OPP (3)Relief. MACT No.1373/2016 Page 2 5 . During the course of proceedings, interim compensation amount was awarded by Ld. Predecessor of this Tribunal on 17.07.2017 for Rs. 25,000/-. 6. Since it came on the record by medical documents as well as disability certificate which was to the extent of 100 % and tribunal noted that due to the accidental injuries, petitioner remained in vegetative state, therefore upon an application under Order 32 Rule 5 CPC, Ld. Predecessor of this tribunal vide order dated 26.04.2017 appointed father of the petitioner Sh. Gulshan Bhatia as legal guardian/next friend of petitioner on the ground that she is 100% disable. 7. In order to prove her case, the petitioner examined five witnesses under: (i) PW1 is Kuldeep S/o Babulal who is eye witness to the accident and deposed regarding the manner in which accident took place. and further stated that immediately after the accident they were taken to Dr.Hedgewar Arogya Sansthan where MLC of him as well as of his son no.422/2017 and 421/2017 were prepared. Witness proved his medical treatment record as Ex.PW1/1, medical bills as Ex.PW1/2, Aadhar card as Ex.PW1/3 and attested copy of DAR as Ex.PW1/4. PW1 stated that accident took place due to rash and negligent driving of driver of tempo no.DL 1LV 1735. (ii) PW-2 is Gulshan Bhatia father of the petitioner, who testify regarding the accident, nature of injuries suffered by the petitioner as well as regarding the medical expenses, and other expenses incurred on account of the injuries of the petitioenor and the fact that petitioner due to head injuries, is 100% disabled and in a vegetative condition. Deepika Bhatiya vs Pulkit Aggarwal on 31 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/133991702/ 2 MACT No.1373/2016 Page 3 (iii) PW3 is Dr. P P Singh, and PW-4 DR Dinesh Kumar Stai from GTB hospital both of them have deposed regarding disability certificate of the petitioner Deepika Bhatia. (iv) PW-5 is Sh.Tushar Diwan from Tata Consultancy Services, who proved the salaries slips of Deepika Bhatia from January 2015 to July 2015. 8. On the other hand, no evidence has been led either on behalf of respondent no.1 and 2 or on behalf of respondent no. 3/ insurance.
texts.arguments: It is submitted that even site plan annexed with the DAR also indicate that accident took place in the middle of the road clearly showing that injured was crossing the road in violation of traffic rules and accident took place in middle of the road. As such injured/petitioner is liable for contributory negligence to the extent of 50%. 12. Ld. Counsel for the petitioner on the other hand submitted that evidence of PW1 as well as other evidence on the record clearly establish rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle by respondent no.1. 13. Contributory negligence consists of the absence of that ordinary care which a sentient being ought Deepika Bhatiya vs Pulkit Aggarwal on 31 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/133991702/ 3 reasonably to have taken for his own safety, and which had it been exercised would have enable him to avoid the injury of which he complains, or the doing of some act which he ought not to have done and but for which the calamity would not have occurred. Wakelin v. London and South Western Ry. Co. (1886) 12 AC 41. The basic principles of Contributory negligence in the field of accident under the MACT No.1373/2016 Page 5 Motor Vehicle Act is that when the defendants prove that the plaintiff has failed to take precautions against the possible danger and that those precautions, if taken, would have been effective to protect against the danger which occurred. "A motorist who drives straight across a light-controlled crossing against the red light and knocks down a pedestrian who has begun to cross in reliance on the lights but without looking over his right shoulder cannot be heard to say that the pedestrian is thereby guilty of Contributory negligence as against him, though such conduct on the part of the pedestrian might attract that description if he had been knocked down by a motorist lawfully turning left with the green light in his favour." A man is not compensated for the physical injury, he is Deepika Bhatiya vs Pulkit Aggarwal on 31 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/133991702/ 5 compensated for the loss which he suffers as a result of that injury (Baker v. Willoughby (1970) Ac 467 at page 492 per Lord Reid). COMPUTATION OF COMPENSATION 21. The scope of compensation in injury cases has been considered by Hon'ble Supreme Court in case titled as Mr. R.D. Hattangadi v. M/s Pest Control (India) Pvt. Ltd., 1995 AIR 755. The relevant extract is as under: "Broadly speaking while fixing an amount of compensation payable to a victim of an accident, the damages have to be assessed separately as pecuniary damages and special damages. Pecuniary damages are those which the victim has actually incurred and which is capable of being calculated in terms of money-, whereas non-pecuniary damages are those which are incapable of being assessed by arithmetical calculations. In order to appreciate two concepts pecuniary damages may, include expenses incurred by the claimant: (i) medical attendance; (ii) MACT No.1373/2016 Page 9 loss of earning of profit upto the date of trial; (iii) other material loss. So far non- pecuniary damages are concerned, they may include (i) damages for mental and physical shock, pain suffering, already suffered or likely to be suffered in future; (ii) damages to compensate for the loss of amenities of life which may include a variety of matters i.e. on account of injury the claimant may not be able to walk, run or sit; (iii) damages for the loss of expectation of life, i.e. on account of injury the normal longevity of the person concerned is shortened; (iv) inconvenience, discomfort, disappointment, hardship, frustration and mental stress in life." 22. Further, in Raj Kumar v. Ajay Kumar & another (2011) 1 SCC 343, Hon'ble Supreme Court of India laid down general principles for computation of compensation in injury cases. The relevant paras of the judgment are reproduced as under: 4. The provisions of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 ("the Act", for short) makes it clear that the award must be just, which means that compensation should, to the extent possible, fully and adequately restore the claimant to the position prior to the accident. The object of awarding damages is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done as far as money can do so, in a fair, reasonable and equitable manner. A person is not only to be compensated for the physical injury, but also for the loss which he suffered as a result of such injury. 5. The heads under which compensation is awarded in personal injury cases are the following: 28. In case of Raj Kumar v. Ajay Kumar & Anr. (2011) 1 SCC 343 , Hon'ble Supreme Court of India determined the broad criteria for assessment of permanent disability for ascertaining the purpose of future loss of earning and also laid down that while assessing the permanent disability of an injured of road side accident, Tribunal must assess the disablement affecting the functioning of the injured, in the light of the work/ service/activities in which injured is involved for his livelihood. In death cases, the MACT No.1373/2016 Page 14 guidelines for computation of compensation have been laid down by Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Sarla Verma and Others v. Delhi Transport Corporation & Anr. (2009) 6 Supreme Court Cases 121. Further, the guidelines have been reiterated by the Constitution Bench of Hon'ble Supreme Court in a case titled as National Insurance Company vs. Pranay Sethi & Ors. Decided on 31.10.2017, laying down the general principles for computation of compensation in death cases. An appropriate multiplier has to be determined for computation of compensation in terms of judgment titled as Sarla Verma v. DTC (2009) 6 SCC 121 which is 15. In view of the judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Pranay Sethi & Others (Supra), in the present case injured is entitled for future prospects to the extent of 50% as injured is below 40 years of age at the time of accident. Petitioner is not only entitled for above amount, but is also entitled for future attendant charges, in view MACT No.1373/2016 Page 17 of the judgment as relied upon by ld. counsel for petitioner of Hon'ble High Court in Pritam Singh vs. Oriental Insurance Co. & Ors. 2016 SCC OnLine Del 2147, wherein it is held that in case where the injured has suffered 100% permanent disability, there can be no doubt that even in future also attendant would be required throughout life and Hon'ble High Court awarded future attendant charges on the basis of minimum wages of unskilled worker. In the present case also injured is 100% permanently disabled and would be dependent on attendant for her future life also. Therefore petitioner in the opinion of this Tribunal is also entitled for future charges for minimum wages of unskilled worker i.e. Rs.10,440/- X 12 X 15 which is Rs.18,79,200/-. While discussing the criteria to ascertain the compensation for pain and sufferings by victim of vehicular accident, observations of Hon'ble High Court of Delhi in Satya Narain v. Jai Kishan, FAO No: 709/02, date of decision: 02.02.2007 can be considered:
